The full repurchase leg remains intact, and the continuous sales-growth rank attenuates rather than eliminates issuance penalties for growing firms, preserving short-side information and portfolio breadth.

considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(MAX(SUB(dlc, che), SUB(ABS(SUB(dlc, che)), ABS(SUB(dlc, che)))), at)))))

considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MUL(MAX(NEG(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))))

considered.name: Undercovered-Payout Issuance Penalty
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MUL(MAX(NEG(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), INDICATOR(SUB(dvt, ib), 0)))))

considered.reasoning: This replaces the weak cash-depletion mechanism with a payout-funding short-side interaction that cannot penalize net repurchasers. Issuance remains adverse for all firms and receives an additional penalty only when dividends are not covered by earnings, while the continuous sales-yield leg maintains stable portfolio breadth.

considered.name: Continuous Debt-Service Capacity Timing
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, dlc), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Repurchases and issuance should convey more valuation information as operating earnings provide greater capacity to meet current debt.

considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms should outperform when equity retirement is clean rather than offset by simultaneous gross issuance.
considered.reasoning: The overlap between gross repurchases and gross issuance measures equity churn that a net-repurchase signal treats as equivalent to clean retirement. Penalizing this overlap distinguishes genuine ownership contraction from buybacks that merely absorb compensation-related or other concurrent dilution.

considered.name: Unretained Equity Issuance Penalty
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), RATIO(MIN(MAX(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(ABS(SUB(sstk, prstkc)), ABS(SUB(sstk, prstkc)))), MAX(SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(ceq, 1)), SUB(ABS(SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(ceq, 1))), ABS(SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(ceq, 1)))))), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuance should be especially adverse when the proceeds are not retained as growth in common equity.
considered.reasoning: The additional penalty is capped by positive net issuance and by the portion of that issuance not reflected in the change in common equity. This uses the accounting link between equity financing and book capital while leaving repurchasers and issuance that remains on the balance sheet unaffected.

considered.name: Dividend-Layered Buyback Surplus
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(MUL(RATIO(prstkc, at), INDICATOR(MIN(dvt, LAG(dvt, 1)), 0)), RATIO(sstk, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms should receive stronger repurchase credit when buybacks are layered on top of an established positive dividend policy.

Gross issuance remains fully adverse, and the continuous sales-yield leg prevents non-dividend payers from collapsing into an event-only portfolio.

considered.name: Concurrent Dual-Claim Retirement
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(MIN(prstkc, MAX(NEG(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), SUB(ABS(NEG(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1))), ABS(NEG(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)))))), sstk), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms should outperform when they simultaneously retire equity and reduce debt, indicating surplus internal funding rather than a leveraged buyback.
considered.reasoning: The minimum operator credits only the dollar amount jointly supported by gross repurchases and an actual decline in total debt, so pure deleveraging cannot drive the signal. Issuance remains fully adverse, while balance-sheet debt changes preserve better coverage than sparsely reported debt-flow fields.

considered.name: Persistent Equity Policy Confirmation
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(ADD(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), RATIO(SUB(MIN(prstkc, LAG(prstkc, 1)), MIN(sstk, LAG(sstk, 1))), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms with repeated repurchases should outperform, while expensive firms with repeated issuance should underperform more reliably than firms undertaking one-time transactions.
considered.reasoning: Current net financing remains fully represented, and the minimum of current and lagged gross flows adds a persistence bonus or penalty only when the same policy continues across periods. This avoids the large neutral bucket of the earlier concordance gate while testing financing-policy commitment with only one lag.

critic_notes.rationale: The MIN "weakest-link" intersection of book-to-market and net repurchase intensity is internally consistent and sign-coherent, but it is a fairly mechanical composite of two extensively published anomalies (value and net share issuance) and its asymmetry (top decile = true intersection, bottom decile = union of either expensive or issuing firms) means the short leg's economics will be muddled.

The sign-alignment gate is internally consistent (cheap-and-shrinking keeps positive exposure, expensive-and-issuing keeps negative exposure, discordant firms are zeroed), giving a genuine conditional rather than additive design, though it remains a confirmation-filtered earnings yield and will lose roughly half its cross-section to the neutralized bucket, risking thin and unstable tails.

The multiplier at/(at + sstk − prstkc) is unstable and can explode or change sign when net repurchases approach assets, and more damningly it amplifies *negative* cash-flow yields for heavy repurchasers — pushing exactly the firms the hypothesis calls undervalued deeper into the short leg — so the expression contradicts the stated mechanism and winsorization only masks the problem.

Netting change in total debt out of equity retirement is a substantive refinement that separates genuine payout capacity from leveraged buybacks (essentially a net-external-financing leg crossed with EV/EBITDA cheapness), and both legs are sign-coherent with the positive expected sign, though the financing leg overlaps meaningfully with the published net-external-financing anomaly.

This is a cosmetic variant of "Weak-Link Value Confirmation" — same MIN intersection of a price-scaled value ratio with net repurchases, differing only by swapping book for sales, ranks for z-scores, and adding a 3-period moving average — so it adds no distinct mechanism and would largely duplicate that signal's evidence.

The expression and negative expected sign are internally consistent and the overvaluation-plus-issuance mechanism is economically clean, but it is close to the documented interaction between market-to-book/market-timing and composite issuance, and because MIN only sharply identifies the short leg, the long leg is an ill-defined union of cheap-or-repurchasing firms that may dilute the long-short alpha.

This reuses exactly the two components of the archived "Issuance-at-a-Premium Trap" (price-to-sales z and net issuance z) and merely swaps MIN for a concordance-gated sum, making it a cosmetic re-aggregation of an already-tested pair that itself restates the well-documented composite-issuance/value interaction.

Decomposing gross repurchases and gross issuance and activating each only in the valuation regime where market timing is plausible is a genuinely different construction from the archived netted MIN composites, the sign logic matches the expression (positive = cheap repurchaser, negative = expensive issuer), and the neutral zero region is economically defensible rather than an artifact.

The structure is identical to the archived "Balance-Sheet-Safe Retirement" (MIN of a cheapness z-score and a net-security-retirement z-score) with only two ingredient substitutions (EBITDA/EV→OCF/P, Δdebt→dltr−dltis), so it is a variant of an already-tested mechanism and close to the known net-external-financing anomaly, with the added risk that dltr/dltis reporting gaps shrink coverage.

The dynamic valuation-response framing is substantively different from the archived static-level composites and the sign logic is internally consistent, but NEG(DELTA(price-to-sales)) is largely a repackaged past-price-change term, so any result must be checked against plain momentum/reversal before being credited to management timing.

This is architecturally the same as the archived "Cash-Supported Financing Confirmation" — a continuous scaled-by-market-cap balance-sheet/cash-flow z-score plus a financing z-score gated on a cash-adequacy condition — with oancf/P swapped for che/P and the gate moved from OCF sign to industry-relative cash, and its base leg is the known cash-holdings/cash-to-price effect.

This is essentially published shareholder/owner yield, and because oancf typically dwarfs net repurchases in dollar magnitude the signal will be numerically dominated by plain cash-flow-to-price, so it is both a rediscovery and too trivial a re-scaling of the archived net-distribution ratio to be informative.

The expression is internally coherent and the binary-to-continuous reweighting (applied only to the financing leg, preserving EBITDA yield for all firms) addresses a real portfolio-stability concern, but it remains a fairly incremental reparameterization of the archive's already-strong maturity-screened signal rather than a new mechanism.

Imposing a temporal sequence (deleveraging first, buyback second) is an economically substantive distinction from the archive's concurrent debt-netting version and the expression correctly implements it, though the two-year-stale conditioner and the complete suppression of the issuance penalty for non-deleveraging firms are real weaknesses.

The |z|-based weight amplifies the financing leg symmetrically at both valuation extremes, so it also rewards expensive repurchasers and penalizes cheap issuers — a broader object than the stated sign-matched hypothesis — while the MA(3)/VOL(5) history requirements will materially thin coverage and the double-rank product is opaque enough that any result would be hard to attribute.

The positive/negative-part decomposition is correctly coded and matches the hypothesis, but it reuses the exact functional form of the archived cash-supported confirmation signal with sales growth swapped for the cash-flow sign, and the premise that buybacks are only credible when sales are growing runs against the usual value-repurchase logic.

Reusing dividends as a discretion screen rather than a favorable payout term is a sensible diagnosis-driven pivot, but with many zero-dividend firms the below-industry-mean indicator will pass a large majority of the cross-section, leaving the screen close to inactive and the signal close to a plain value-plus-net-repurchase sum.

The second leg subtracts a percentage share-count growth from an assets-scaled cash flow, so the much larger-variance GROWTH(csho) term will dominate, reducing the signal to a standard rank composite of EV/EBITDA value and the published net-share-issuance anomaly rather than the intended repurchase-execution corroboration.

This is a conditioner swap on the already-archived Maturity-Weighted Financing Discretion template (value z + payout z × IND_RANK(conditioner)) with a highly correlated liquidity proxy, and the stated mechanism ("cash exceeds current debt") is not actually what an industry rank of (che−dlc)/at identifies, since rank conveys relative position rather than sign.

Same archived additive-interaction template with profitability substituted as the conditioner, which both amounts to a value-plus-quality-plus-payout composite (well-trodden ground) and contradicts its own hypothesis, since IND_RANK(ib/at) does not isolate "positive profitability" and can assign high weights to loss-making firms in weak industries.

A purely cosmetic binary-to-continuous recoding of the archived Flexible-Payout Value Timing signal within the archived Maturity-Weighted structure; no new economic mechanism is introduced and the resulting signal will be nearly collinear with both predecessors.

The positive-part debt adjustment is a well-motivated and correctly implemented fix (MAX(x, ABS(x)−ABS(x)) = max(x,0)) that isolates debt-funded repurchases from pure deleveraging, distinguishing it economically from the archived MIN-based Balance-Sheet-Safe Retirement, though it remains adjacent to known net-external-financing anomalies.

The sign logic is internally consistent (repurchases up-weighted by cheapness, issuance penalized more when expensive) and it substantively repairs the diagnosed flaws of the earlier gross-flow, hard-cutoff version, though the interaction leg partially double-counts the additive valuation leg and this self-conditioning should be checked for redundancy.

A genuine, correctly coded asymmetric refinement of the archived post-deleveraging signal — the issuance penalty is no longer inadvertently switched off by the same indicator that gates the repurchase reward — with a hypothesis that matches what the expression computes.

The positive-part construction is correct and the "capitalize only uncovered current debt" denominator is an untested variant of the archived EV-style value legs, but the financing leg is the plain generation-0 net-repurchase z-score, so the incremental content is confined to a modest denominator tweak.

This is a mechanical additive stack of two already-evaluated financing legs (Residual-Liquidity Buyback Feasibility and Debt-Increase-Only Repurchase Quality) on the identical ebitda/market-cap value leg, offering no new economic mechanism and risking double-penalizing the same debt-financed buybacks.

Replacing the binary prior-deleveraging gate with continuous lagged deleveraging intensity is a legitimate, diagnosis-motivated refinement with correct sign behavior (non-negative rank weight preserves the issuance penalty), though structurally it is the same ADD(value, MUL(financing, IND_RANK)) template as the archive's strongest signal with only the conditioning variable swapped.

The construction matches the hypothesis and the conditional application of the cash-depletion penalty is sensibly restricted to net repurchasers, but since buybacks mechanically drain cash the penalty may largely cancel the repurchase signal itself rather than isolate funding quality.

A genuinely different use-of-proceeds mechanism that mirrors prior work on the issuance rather than repurchase side, and the negative-part construction is correct—though it fully neutralizes rather than merely shrinks the penalty as the hypothesis states, and neutralizing the issuance leg may sacrifice the short-side power that drives the archive's better results.

A coherent flow-affordability analog of the archived residual-liquidity gate, but the ib − dvt − prstkc > 0 condition will systematically exclude the most aggressive repurchasers (whose gross buybacks routinely exceed retained earnings), potentially gating out the very group carrying the signal.

The expression correctly restricts the positive-debt-growth penalty to net repurchasers (MAX(ΔDebt,0) gated by INDICATOR of net repurchase) and matches its hypothesis, but it is a narrow permutation of the already-tested "Debt-Increase-Only Repurchase Quality" / "Balance-Sheet-Safe Retirement" family and will likely be highly correlated with them.

The soft rank-weighted issuance penalty is internally consistent (penalty largest when debt is rising, near zero when debt falls) and the binary→continuous gating change has precedent for materially improving portfolio evidence in this archive, though it remains an incremental re-parameterization of "Non-Deleveraging Issuance Penalty."

The expression reduces to value + fin×(1+rank) versus the archived best's value + fin×rank, i.e. a monotone rescaling that is a near-linear combination of two already-tested signals and should be almost perfectly correlated with them, making it a cosmetic variant rather than a substantive test.

The flow-based EBITDA coverage gate is economically distinct from the archived stock-liquidity and net-income gates, but it is the third member of the same gate-the-gross-repurchase family and simultaneously swaps the value proxy to sale/mktcap, confounding attribution of any improvement.

This correctly diagnoses the mechanical flaw in the archived cash-preservation signal (buybacks necessarily reduce cash) and implements a coherent, non-cosmetic fix that penalizes only depletion in excess of the repurchase outlay, with the expression matching the stated hypothesis and sign.

The continuous residual-earnings scaling is internally consistent and plausibly repairs the hard gate that dropped large repurchasers, though the rank multiplier also shrinks the repurchase leg relative to the unscaled issuance penalty, an asymmetry not addressed in the hypothesis.

The expression is internally consistent and the dollar-matched cap is economically sensible, but it is the third pass over the same "subtract positive debt growth from the net-repurchase leg" knob already tested unconditionally (gen3, ls_talpha 2.89) and repurchase-gated (gen5, ls_talpha 3.32), so it reads as a cosmetic refinement rather than a new mechanism.

This is a straightforward stacking of the archive's best signal (rank-weighted dlc discretion, ls_talpha 3.82) with the capped debt-funding purge, and while the two legs are genuinely distinct (stock constraint vs. funding flow) the incremental information content over the existing pair is likely small.

A clean, scale-consistent absolute-coverage gate that plausibly diagnoses whether the maturity effect is about debt-service capacity rather than a cross-sectional dlc rank, though a binary EBITDA>dlc dummy will hold for the large majority of firms and so may barely differ from the ungated value-plus-issuance composite.

The construction does exactly what the hypothesis says (issuance attenuated dollar-for-dollar by debt reduction, repurchasers untouched), but it is the third functional form applied to the identical issuance-side deleveraging offset already tested as a binary gate (gen4) and a rank weight (gen5), both of which underperformed the repurchase-side refinements.

Replacing the binary residual-liquidity gate with a monotone dollar cap is a substantive construction change that fixes a real information-discarding flaw, the positive-part guard correctly prevents manufactured capacity from negative surplus, and the sign logic matches the expression.

The asymmetric rank weighting is correctly signed for both the repurchase and issuance legs and targets a different conditioning variable than the earlier soft-rank experiment, but the archive already shows that softening a hard gate (gen3 Soft Two-Sided Financing Timing) destroyed the portfolio alpha, so the expected gain over the gen2 hard-sign version is questionable and the near-full forgiveness of issuance by high-growth firms deserves a robustness check.

This is a mechanical recombination of two things already in the archive — the maturity-rank conditioner from "Maturity-Weighted Financing Discretion" (alpha 0.042, t=3.82) and the positive/negative-part asymmetry template already applied in "Debt-Use Issuance Attenuation" and "Revenue-Absorption Issuance Test" — so it is a cosmetic decomposition rather than a new mechanism, and by construction it can only shrink the archived signal's conditioning.

The exact mirror of the preceding proposal (their weighted parts sum back to the archived maturity-weighted signal), it is again a cosmetic asymmetric split of an existing best performer, and its economic story is weaker — low current debt as a marker of "discretionary" issuance conflicts with the more standard reading that distressed, high-short-debt issuers are the ones that underperform.

Replacing gross dlc/at with uncovered current debt max(dlc−che,0)/at is a genuine and economically better-motivated change to the conditioning state of the archive's strongest mechanism, though the positive-part construction leaves a large mass of firms at exactly zero, so IND_RANK will produce a coarse, tie-heavy conditioner that may blunt rather than sharpen the archived result.

Pairing the liquidity-capped repurchase leg with a distinct structural-solvency rank is a defensible non-redundant extension of an archived signal, but multiplying the whole financing z-score by NEG(lt/at) rank also attenuates the issuance short leg precisely for high-leverage issuers — the group most likely to underperform — which works against the hypothesis and risks weakening the alpha it aims to improve.

The construction is internally incoherent: the archived organic-book leg worked because Δceq mechanically contains net equity issuance (a clean accounting identity), whereas Δsale does not, so subtracting issuance dollars from a revenue change is an arbitrary mixing of incommensurable quantities that mostly reduces to a value tilt plus the well-known net-share-issuance anomaly.

The expression faithfully implements the stated hypothesis and the organic-book gate is a legitimate accounting-identity-based validation of buybacks, but it is a fairly predictable splice of two archived constructs (the organic-book leg and the gated-gross-repurchase-minus-sstk template), so incremental information over those is likely modest.

Because IND_RANK is a monotone transform, dropping the positive-part truncation only breaks ties among cash-surplus firms, making this a near-cosmetic re-run of the archived "Cash-Adjusted Maturity Discretion" (and third variant of the same maturity-weighted financing family) rather than a substantively new mechanism.

Restricting the solvency weight to the capped repurchase leg while preserving the full gross-issuance penalty is a legitimate, diagnosis-motivated asymmetry rather than a pure rescaling of the archived solvency-weighted signal, though the expected incremental gain over talpha 3.26 is modest.

The stated mechanism (penalize issuance that coincides with cash depletion, leaving repurchases untouched) contradicts the expression, since MIN(sstk/at, cash-depletion⁺) is strictly positive for the many net repurchasers that have nonzero gross issuance and declining cash — precisely the firms buybacks mechanically deplete — and this cash-depletion family already delivered near-zero alpha in the archive.

Dollar-capping the maturity-migration penalty at gross repurchases is an economically sensible bound on an already-strong archived signal, but it simultaneously changes the gate from net-repurchaser to any-gross-repurchaser without acknowledging that, so it is an incremental refinement whose incremental content is small.

Replacing the archived all-or-nothing organic-book gate with a dollar cap is a coherent, accounting-consistent graduation that preserves partial credit for aggressive repurchasers, though it recombines two already-tested devices (organic book accretion and dollar capping) rather than introducing a new mechanism.

Relocating the net-liquidity conditioner from the financing leg to the valuation leg is a genuinely distinguishable design that discriminates between the "distress value trap" and "financing discretion" interpretations of the archive's best result, and the sign logic is consistent (nonnegative rank shrinks, never flips, the value score).

Internally coherent and correctly signed, but it is the third re-weighting of the same EBITDA-yield-plus-net-repurchase core by a liquidity/maturity rank (Maturity-Weighted Financing Discretion, Cash-Adjusted Maturity Discretion), and MIN of two highly correlated balance-sheet ranks is unlikely to add information beyond the already-tested net-current-debt version.

This is a mechanical mash-up of two archived signals (Liquidity-Capped Repurchase Credit and Maturity-Weighted Financing Discretion) and is structurally identical to Solvency-Weighted Liquidity Repurchase with dlc/at swapped for lt/at, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.
